$comment: Primary-source oracle — individual-filer cases: 2026 enhanced senior deduction phaseout boundaries and the SSA retirement earnings test. Expected values derived independently from the cited sources; never from production code.

irs-senior-deduction.name: IRS — Check your eligibility for the new enhanced deduction for seniors
irs-senior-deduction.identifier: $6,000 per eligible individual 65+, tax years 2025-2028; phases out for MAGI over $75,000 ($150,000 joint); Pub. L. 119-21 §70103 phase-out rate 6%

irs-ir-2025-103.name: IRS IR-2025-103 — tax year 2026 annual inflation adjustments (with Rev. Proc. 2025-32)
irs-ir-2025-103.identifier: 2026 Single ordinary brackets and $16,100 standard deduction; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 §2.15 additional standard deduction $2,050 (unmarried, 65+)

ssa-rtea-2026.name: SSA Office of the Chief Actuary — Exempt Amounts Under the Earnings Test
ssa-rtea-2026.publication: 2026 amounts announced with the SSA 2026 COLA determination (October 2025)
ssa-rtea-2026.accessed: 2026-07-24 (via Internet Archive snapshot of 2026-07-02; the live page rejects non-browser clients)
ssa-rtea-2026.identifier: 2026 lower exempt amount $24,480 ($1 withheld per $2 over); higher (FRA-year) exempt amount $65,160 ($1 per $3 over)

poms-rs-02501-030.name: SSA POMS RS 02501.030 — Applying the Monthly Earnings Test (MET) (implements 20 C.F.R. §404.435)
poms-rs-02501-030.identifier: The MET applies when an entitled beneficiary has one or more non-service months in a grace year: full benefit payable for a non-service month (earnings at/below the monthly limit = 1/12 of the annual exempt amount); a service month's check is withheld

usc-86.name: 26 U.S.C. §86 — taxation of Social Security benefits (base amounts + tier composition)
usc-86.publication: statutory (OLRC current edition; base amounts fixed since 1993)
usc-86.identifier: Single base $25,000 / adjusted base $34,000 (§86(c)(1)(A)); provisional income = modified AGI + tax-exempt interest (§86(b)(2)(B)) + 1/2 benefits; 50% tier = lesser of 1/2 benefits and 1/2 the excess over the base; 85% tier above the adjusted base

ssa-fra-1959.name: SSA — Retirement age chart (42 U.S.C. §416(l) full-retirement-age schedule)
ssa-fra-1959.identifier: Born 1959 -> FRA 66 years 10 months (802 months); born 1960+ -> 67

cases.description: Single filer age 66, ordinary income $50,000 (below the $75,000 phaseout base): full $6,000 senior deduction.
Single filer age 66, MAGI exactly $75,000 (at the phaseout base): still the full $6,000.
derivation: MAGI 75,000: phaseout applies only to the excess OVER the base -> max(0, 75,000-75,000)*6% = 0 -> deduction 6,000.

cases.description: Single filer age 66, MAGI $95,000 (above the base): deduction phased down by 6% of the $20,000 excess.
Single filer age 66, MAGI $180,000 (at/above $175,000 the deduction is fully phased out).
Pre-FRA-year annual earnings test, 2026: $1 withheld per $2 of earnings over the $24,480 lower exempt amount.
cases.tolerance: exact ($1-per-$2 statutory rule on exact exempt amounts; month counts exact)
derivation: Beneficiary born 1962-03-10 -> FRA 67 reached March 2029, so 2026 is a pre-FRA year.

Gross benefit 18,000/yr = 1,500/mo uniform checks; charging fills whole checks from January: 5 full checks (7,500) + a 500 partial in June -> 6 withheld months (a partially withheld check is a non-payment month).

cases.description: Grace-year monthly non-service test, 2026: full benefit for each non-service month (earnings <= $24,480/12 = $2,040); the more favorable test wins.
derivation: Annual test would withhold min(24,000, (80,000-24,480)/2 = 27,760) = 24,000 (every check).
Monthly test withholds only the 8 service-month checks: 8 * 2,000 = 16,000; the smaller withholding wins -> 16,000 withheld, 8,000 payable, 8 withheld months.

cases.description: FRA-year earnings test, 2026: born 1959-05-10 (FRA 66y10m -> March 2026); $1 withheld per $3 of pre-FRA-month earnings over the $65,160 higher exempt amount.
cases.tolerance: exact ($1-per-$3 statutory rule on the exact higher exempt amount; month counts exact)
derivation: Born 1959-05-10 -> FRA 66y10m (SSA schedule): 1959*12 + 4 + 802 = 24,314 months -> FRA reached March 2026 (month index 2), so 2026 is the FRA year and only January + February earnings count (20 C.F.R. §404.430).

Gross benefit 24,000/yr = 2,000/mo checks; only the two pre-FRA checks (4,000) are chargeable; charging fills January's whole 2,000 check -> 1 withheld month; benefits from March on are untouched (the test stops at FRA).

cases.description: Pre-FRA year, 2026 earnings below the $24,480 lower exempt amount: no excess, nothing withheld, no months charged.
derivation: Beneficiary born 1962-03-10 -> 2026 is a pre-FRA year (FRA 67 reached March 2029).
Earnings 20,000 <= 24,480 -> excess 0 -> withholding $0, 0 withheld months, full 18,000 benefit payable.

cases.description: §86(a)(1) none tier: provisional income at/below the $25,000 Single base amount -> $0 of benefits taxable.
derivation: Gross SS 20,000; other AGI 12,000; no tax-exempt interest -> provisional income = 12,000 + 10,000 = 22,000 <= 25,000.

cases.description: §86(a)(2)(A) 50% tier where HALF THE EXCESS over the base binds inside the min() (the smaller of the two 50% terms).
§86(a)(2)(A) 50% tier where HALF THE GROSS BENEFIT binds inside the min() (the other arm of the composition).
derivation: Gross SS 4,000; other AGI 29,000 -> provisional income = 29,000 + 2,000 = 31,000, in (25,000, 34,000].

cases.description: §86(b)(2)(B): tax-exempt (muni) interest is added back to provisional income — here the add-back alone lifts the household from the none tier into the 50% tier.
derivation: Gross SS 20,000; other AGI 14,000; tax-exempt interest 4,000 -> provisional income = 14,000 + 4,000 + 10,000 = 28,000, in (25,000, 34,000].
Without the §86(b)(2)(B) add-back, provisional income would be 24,000 <= 25,000 -> tier none, $0 — the add-back changes both the tier and the amount, so a dropped add-back cannot pass.
